articles.title: Where to watch Friday Night Baseball on Apple TV: Phillies vs. Mets start time and more
articles.summary: The Mets host the Phillies for this week's Friday Night Baseball game on Apple TV. Here's how to watch.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies will be spending the weekend in Queens where they're playing the New York Mets in a four-game series at Citi Field. The second game of the series will be part of Apple TV's Friday Night Baseball broadcast and will be available exclusively on the streaming platform. Expect to see Jesus Luzardo starting on the pitcher's mound for the Phillies; Zac Thornton will be the Mets' starting pitcher in Friday's game, The Phillies vs. Mets game will begin at 7:15 p.m. ET.

The teams will finish their series with games on Saturday and Sunday, all at Citi Field.

Here's what you need to know so you can watch the Phillies vs. Mets on Friday and learn the rest of their weekend schedule.

How to watch the Philadelphia Phillies vs. New York Mets game:

When is the Philadelphia Phillies vs. New York Mets game?

The Friday Night Baseball game between the Phillies and the Mets is Friday, Sept. 19 at 7:15 p.m. ET.

What channel will the Phillies vs. Mets game be on?

The Phillies vs. Mets game will be broadcast on Apple TV.

How to watch the Philadelphia Phillies vs. New York Mets without cable

The Phillies vs. Mets game will stream exclusively on Apple TV.

1:10 p.m.: Phillies @ Mets (WPIX, NBCSP)

articles.title: Ranking Kevin McGonigle, Sal Stewart and Every MLB Team's Best Rookie in 2026
articles.summary: Major League Baseball's 2026 rookie class has been one of the strongest in recent history.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball's 2026 rookie class has been one of the strongest in recent history.

Put Brewers pitcher Logan Henderson in a time machine to last season, and he could win NL Rookie of the Year. Send White Sox outfielder Tristan Peters back to 2024 and he probably wins AL Rookie of the Year in unanimous fashion. They both might be headed for fifth-place finishes in this year's star-studded races.

Ahead, we've ranked each team's best rookie from No. 30 up to No. 1.

In several cases—most notably with the Pittsburgh Pirates and the New York Mets—it was difficult to decide which of the multiple viable candidates was the team's best rookie.

Overall, though, that was the easy part. Figuring out the proper order of the top dozen rookies was the real challenge.

Even if you don't concur with some of the rankings, hopefully we can all agree that once MLB and the MLBPA get this next collective bargaining agreement sorted out, the future of baseball is looking great.

Nos. 30-26: Gray, Anderson, Freeland, Painter and Blubaugh

It's mighty slim pickens from the Rangers, who have used just one rookie hitter (Cam Cauley) and a handful of rookie relievers. This particular rookie reliever was already 30 years old before making his MLB debut. Gray did provide some value, though, going 6-0 with eight holds and a 3.93 ERA before landing on the IL with elbow inflammation.

It's almost certainly too little, too late, but the Mariners finally got desperate enough to start calling up top prospects a few weeks ago. While Michael Arroyo and Lazaro Montes have both hit the ball well in their limited sample of barely 50 combined plate appearances, Anderson is the one that everyone is most excited about. We are still waiting on him to really showcase his elite strikeout stuff, though.

28. 2B Alex Freeland, Los Angeles Dodgers

There's already a case to be made for Josue De Paula in this spot, even though he just made his MLB debut as Shohei Ohtani's fill-in last Friday. However, Freeland spent much of the season as the Dodgers' primary second baseman, providing decent value with his glove while hitting just well enough to earn regular playing time.

27. RHP Andrew Painter, Philadelphia Phillies

After years of hype as a top prospect, Painter didn't exactly deliver the goods out of the gate, posting a 7.06 ERA in his first 14 starts before being sent back to Triple-A. Since his return to the majors at the end of July, though, his ERA has been half of what it used to be, sitting at a mark of 3.58 in his last nine turns through the rotation.

Heading into the season, the expectation was that Tatsuya Imai would be Houston's representative on this list. But while Imai has posted the worst walk rate among all pitchers with at least 40 innings of work, Blubaugh has been quite the asset as a bulk reliever. He doesn't often get used in high-leverage situations, but in 91 innings pitched—most in the majors among players who haven't started any games—he has a 3.26 ERA.

Nos. 25-21: Culpepper, Basallo, Ramirez, Valdez and Jones

25. SS Kaelen Culpepper, Minnesota Twins

Shortstop had been a season-long adventure for the Twins until they called up Culpepper in early August. In just 31 games in the majors, he has already had six multi-hit performances. Among the 70 rookies with at least 100 plate appearances, his .275 batting average ranks 10th. (It's also the second-highest batting average among the 14 Twins with at least 100 PA.)

Basallo has 18 home runs, which is nothing to sneeze at. Only two of those round-trippers have come in the past two months, though, as Basallo has a disastrous .149/.250/.243 triple-slash since the All-Star Break. He was one of the top six or seven preseason candidates for AL Rookie of the Year, but he most likely won't receive a single vote at this rate.

Quite the opposite of Basallo, Ramírez opened the second half with an .865 OPS in his first 34 games. When Dansby Swanson hit the IL in mid-August, it was a no-brainer for Chicago to bump Nico Hoerner over to shortstop while cementing Ramírez as the near-everyday second baseman. Where he fits in a fully healthy Cubs lineup remains to be seen, but he has been a surprisingly key piece of MLB's highest-scoring offense.

22. OF Esmerlyn Valdez, Pittsburgh Pirates

Konnor Griffin or Bubba Chandler could have been the pick for the Pirates, which is good news for the Buccos' future. But Valdez has an .855 OPS, racking up 17 home runs in 287 trips to the plate. That 5.9 percent home run rate matches Matt Olson and is only slightly behind Yordan Alvarez. Not too shabby for a guy who came out of nowhere. ( Steamer didn't have Valdez projected to play in the majors this season.)

With Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger and Trent Grisham missing a combined total of nearly 150 games this season, Jones has gotten considerably more playing time than expected heading into the year. Though he hasn't come close to matching the 35 HR, 29 SB, .932 OPS line he posted in the minors in 2025, it's hard to argue with the .802 OPS he's posted since the beginning of June. Even if Grisham is healthy heading into October, Jones might be New York's primary CF in the postseason.

Nos. 20-16: Rodriguez, Mack, Garcia, Alvarez and Eldridge

20. RHP Bradgley Rodriguez, San Diego Padres

Despite losing Robert Suarez in free agency, the Padres have one of baseball's most unhittable bullpens for a third straight year. Rodriguez posting a 2.38 ERA and 2.86 FIP while filling the Suarez-shaped void has been a massive piece of that puzzle. He has 15 holds and two saves for a team that will most likely make the postseason.

Miami's decision to move Liam Hicks at the trade deadline was a surprise, but also quite the vote of confidence in this rookie catcher. Unfortunately, Mack has struggled at the dish over the past six weeks, but his value added behind the dish has remained strong. Only William Contreras (25) has thrown out more stolen base attempts than Mack's 24.

18. LHP Brandyn Garcia, Arizona Diamondbacks

The Diamondbacks have been reluctant to lock in Garcia as their primary closer, presumably because he is the only left-handed reliever on the active roster. He has been their most dominant relief pitcher, boasting a 1.94 ERA, 0.76 WHIP and 10.7 K/9 in 46.1 innings pitched. In fact, among MLB pitchers with at least 40 innings of work, only Josh Hader (0.65) has a lower WHIP.

17. LHP Andrew Alvarez, Washington Nationals

Foster Griffin was a viable candidate here, even though the Nationals traded him away. Alvarez has picked up the slack since Griffin's departure, posting a 2.44 ERA over his last eight starts to bring his full-season mark down to 3.35. Couple that with the 2.31 ERA he had in his five starts last season, he may remain in the middle of this rotation.

16. 1B/DH Bryce Eldridge, San Francisco Giants

Over the past decade, the Giants have received a grand total of one vote for NL ROY, which went to Patrick Bailey with a third-place vote in 2023. Eldridge has no hope of winning the award, but he should at least get a few down-ballot votes for his .269/.364/.461 triple slash with 17 home runs. They didn't call him up until early May, but he has been one of their most valuable players.

Nos. 15-11: Fuentes, Bolte, Okamoto, Rumfield and Mesa

Shortly after his 20th birthday, Fuentes made four starts for Atlanta last summer, allowing 20 earned runs in 13 innings. Take out his one spot start in April and he has allowed just 13 earned runs in 66.1 innings of work as a reliever this year. Outside of closer Raisel Iglesias, he is the most trusted arm in this bullpen at this point.

Not much has gone right for the A's over the past three months, but Bolte has been a welcome exception. He wasn't a top-100 prospect coming into the season, but a 1.076 OPS in 37 games at Triple-A forced the A's to call him up in mid-May. He has played in almost every game since then, leading the team in both batting average (.275) and stolen bases (20).

13. 3B Kazuma Okamoto, Toronto Blue Jays

Inexplicably, only two Blue Jays have more than 10 home runs: George Springer with 15 and Okamoto, who leads all rookies with 33. Strikeouts and glovework concerns are why he and his big bat had to settle for a four-year, $60M deal in his transition from NPB to MLB. He does have 175 whiffs and 19 errors. But he's been worth every penny, leading the team in runs and RBI.

When it comes to breakout stars for Colorado, you always have to ask: Can he do it on the road, too? In Rumfield's case, yes. He has an OPS of at least .800 at Coors Field and away from it. He boasts a top-10 batting average (.300) among qualified hitters. He also hit .290 over the past two years in the minors, so this hasn't completely come out of nowhere.

Mesa played in 16 big-league games for the Marlins last season, but had a .641 OPS. They traded him to Tampa Bay in February for a 19-year-old infielder. He has been sensational in his new home since mid-July, posting a .961 OPS with 10 home runs over his last 42 games played. Save for Junior Caminero, he has become the Rays' best slugger.

Nos. 10-6: Jensen, Urena, Peters, Tolle and Henderson

Jensen has been on fire lately, batting .318/.430/.788 over his last 18 games. However, that heater comes on the heels of a 42-game stretch in which he hit .160/.278/.307. It's hard to argue with 24 home runs and 59 extra-base hits from your catcher, though. That type of production has been business as usual for the Royals with Salvador Perez over the past 14 years, but it's definitely not the norm.

9. RHP Walbert Ureña, Los Angeles Angels

Though Ureña isn't quite our highest-ranked rookie pitcher, he's been—without a remotely close runner-up—the most valuable pitcher who hadn't appeared in an MLB game prior to this season. Since joining the rotation in mid-April, 12 of his 25 appearances have been quality starts. Well, let's just say we didn't see that coming from a guy who FanGraphs rated in January as the 23rd-best prospect in the Angels' farm system.

Munetaka Murakami is Chicago's highest-profile rookie, but Peters has been the most valuable one. In addition to hitting for the cycle in July, he went five consecutive games in August with a home run and an OPS just shy of .800. There's a good chance he's going to win a Gold Glove for his work in the outfield. Imagine if Tampa Bay hadn't given him away for future considerations back in December.

Say this much for Tolle: No one is having more fun with their rookie season. From the no-brain balk to the hug to the push-up to the immaculate smile , he has rapidly become one of the most likeable players in the sport. Opposing hitters aren't particularly loving him, though, as he has a 3.02 ERA and a 10.4 K/9 en route to what should be a top-three finish for AL ROY.

6. RHP Logan Henderson, Milwaukee Brewers

Because he has only made 17 starts, ranking Henderson was the biggest conundrum of this entire exercise. In those starts, he has a 2.51 ERA, 0.81 WHIP and 10.3 K/9. That makes him one of just five pitchers with at least 80 innings of work, a sub-3.00 ERA, a sub-1.00 WHIP and a 10+ K/9. The others are Jacob Misiorowski, Cam Schlittler, Tarik Skubal and Chris Sale. He's probably going to start Game 2 of the postseason for the Brewers. It's a crime that no one is even talking about him as the possible NL Rookie of the Year.

Season Stats : 166.2 IP, 3.24 ERA, 3.67 FIP, 1.18 WHIP, 9.9 K/9, 2.6 bWAR

Where to rank Logan Henderson was the toughest decision of this exercise, but trying to decide who the Mets' representative ought to be was a close runner-up.

If we were simply ranking the top rookies regardless of team, the Mets would easily have two in the top 10 and possibly four in the top 25.

In particular, Carson Benge presents a compelling case for this spot, boasting 18 home runs, 22 stolen bases and a howitzer of an arm responsible for 10 outfield assists. For all the misfires the Mets had with their offseason moves, betting on Benge in an everyday role definitely hit the mark.

But Nolan McLean is probably going to be the Met who receives the most NL Rookie of the Year votes, blossoming into the undisputed ace of this pitching staff.

He did have a bit of a dud against the Yankees last week, allowing five runs in a loss to the Bronx Bombers. He still has 18 quality starts for the year and entered that one with a 2.24 ERA over his previous 17 starts.

If he finishes strong and reaches 20 quality starts, he would be the first rookie to do so since Yordano Ventura racked up 22 in 2014. But already, 18 puts him in rarefied air. The only pitchers to do that in the past 12 years were Michael Soroka in 2019 (18) and Shota Imanaga in 2024 (19).

Also on the table: McLean is 19 strikeouts away from 203, a mark no rookie has reached since Yu Darvish in 2012.

4. JJ Wetherholt, SS, St. Louis Cardinals

Season Stats : .242/.343/.370, 17 HR, 48 RBI, 14 SB, 4.6 bWAR

JJ Wetherholt has been sidelined by wrist tendinitis since late August, likely ending the debate over whether he or the next player on this list deserves to be NL Rookie of the Year.

In his five healthy months, though, this young Cardinal made quite the first impression.

As the leadoff hitter for pretty much the entire season, RBI opportunities were few and far between. But Wetherholt has been quite the table-setter for Jordan Walker and Alec Burleson to each eclipse 100 RBI, with his .343 on-base percentage translating to 88 runs scored. (Had he not gotten hurt, he would almost certainly rank top 10 in the majors in that department.)

His real value added, however, has been on defense.

Per Statcast, Wetherholt has a Fielding Run Value of 21 and an Outs Above Average rating of 22. He's second to Pete Crow-Armstrong in the former and trails only PCA and Bobby Witt Jr. in the latter.

In 527 chances, this middle infielder has committed just two errors—both in the first two weeks of the season. He's a perfect 467-for-467 since April 11, which is kind of ludicrous.

Season Stats : .269/.338/.472, 31 HR, 108 RBI, 15 SB, 2.3 bWAR

If you're a Blue Jays fan, you might be wondering why in the world this rookie with 31 home runs is 10 spots ahead of your rookie with 33 home runs.

Well, it mostly boils down to one thing: Sal Stewart's clutch gene.

While Kazuma Okamoto has a .676 OPS and 54 RBI in 164 plate appearances with runners in scoring position, Stewart seems to always come through in the clutch, boasting a .949 OPS and 85 RBI in 179 plate appearances with runners in scoring position.

Now, that OPS is nowhere near best in the majors. Both Yordan Alvarez and Nick Kurtz are in the 1.300 range. It's still a remarkable, David Ortiz-like mark from a rookie who's done pretty much all he can to carry an offense that still ranks dead last in the National League in runs scored, in spite of his heroics.

Beyond flirting with becoming the first rookie to lead the majors in RBI since Walt Dropo in 1950, Stewart has simply been a solid overall force on offense. If he can manage three more hits and two more RBI the rest of the way, he'll join 2022 Aaron Judge, 2024 Shohei Ohtani and 2024 José Ramírez as the only players in the 2020s with at least 160 hits, 110 RBI, 30 home runs and 15 stolen bases in the same season.

His Wins Above Replacement rating is nowhere near JJ Wetherholt's, which is going to make for quite the "old school vs. new school" debate for NL Rookie of the Year.

As for me and my house, though, the nod goes to the guy with more than twice as many RBI as the one with a great glove at second base.

2. Parker Messick, LHP, Cleveland Guardians

Season Stats : 178.1 IP, 2.57 ERA, 3.11 FIP, 1.04 WHIP, 9.4 K/9, 5.7 bWAR

Do you know what is irrationally fun about Parker Messick's dominance?

Per Statcast , his fastball run value ranks in the 99th percentile with a rating of +36. Only Jacob Misiorowski ranks ahead of him at +37.

While you probably expect that type of grade from The Miz and his 105 MPH heaters, Messick's four-seamer maxes out at around 97 MPH, barely averaging 94 MPH. He's actually below league average in fastball velocity, but there's just something about his release angle and his Gumby-like delivery that makes it tough to hit.

You might now be thinking, "Well, you don't need a flamethrower of a fastball if you have elite breaking pitches, so he must have some phenomenal secondary offerings."

*Insert jarring game show buzzer noise for incorrect answers here*

Messick routinely throws six pitches, but opponents are slugging .629 against his slider, .735 against his curveball and .750 against his cutter. Even wilder, he has thrown his curveball 245 times and recorded just one strikeout from it.

But having those in his arsenal keeps the opposition guessing, which keeps his two bread-and-butter pitches (four-seamer and changeup) lethal.

In all but one of his 30 starts, Messick has completed at least five innings. He also has yet to allow more than four earned runs in a start, even during his seven-start foray into the majors toward the end of last season.

If the Guardians finish this fight and crash the postseason, having Messick and Gavin Williams for Games 1 and 2 could keep them in business for more than just one round.

1. Kevin McGonigle, SS/3B, Detroit Tigers

Season Stats : .273/.373/.425, 17 HR, 65 RBI, 12 SB, 6.7 bWAR

In ranking Sal Stewart ahead of JJ Wetherholt, we've already made it clear that WAR isn't everything.

If all you care about is Baseball-Reference's calculation of wins above replacement for MVP vo tes, say hello to your pick for AL MVP*, as Kevin McGonigle is slightly ahead of both Bobby Witt Jr. (6.3) and Yordan Alvarez (6.1) in that category.

*Actually, Cam Schlittler (7.1) leads the American League in bWAR, but we all know MVP voters don't care about pitchers unless they are named Shohei Ohtani. The last non-Ohtani pitcher to receive even one first-place MVP vote was Jacob deGrom in 2018, and he still finished fifth in the overall vote.

There isn't one particular area where McGonigle dominates the competition, but he has been rock solid across the board.

His plate discipline is next level, top 10 in the majors in walks drawn (91) and one of just a few players with more walks than strikeouts (90).

He doesn't steal much and has gone just 1-for-5 in stolen-base attempts since the beginning of July. However, he is also an exceptional baserunner, leading the majors with 31 bases taken .

Sure, his defense could use some work, but 18 errors while bouncing back and forth between shortstop and third base—including playing both in the same game on 38 occasions —isn't bad. He's the only player this season with at least 55 appearances at both positions, with at least 85 at each. We would love to see what he can do if cemented at one or the other in the future.

McGonigle is going to win AL Rookie of the Year, perhaps unanimously so. Pretty easy choice for No. 1 on this list.

articles.title: “It s*cks to be him”: Kyle Harrison’s Milwaukee Brewers future takes a tough turn as fans react to his struggles
articles.summary: MLB News: Kyle Harrison’s October hopes are getting harder to defend after another difficult outing left the Milwaukee Brewers with more questions than answers..
articles.body: Kyle Harrison’s October hopes are getting harder to defend after another difficult outing left the Milwaukee Brewers with more questions than answers. The 25-year-old left-hander was pulled in the second inning of Thursday’s 7-4 loss to the Pittsburgh Pirates, continuing a rough stretch that has changed his postseason outlook. Kyle Harrison once looked like an important piece of Milwaukee’s pitching plans, but his recent numbers have made that role uncertain. With only nine regular-season games remaining, every appearance now carries extra weight. Brewers manager Pat Murphy has not closed the door on Kyle Harrison, but the lefty has little time left to show that he can still help the team in October.Kyle Harrison’s recent slide has changed the conversation around his October roleThe reaction from Milwaukee Brewers fans showed how quickly the mood has changed around Kyle Harrison. Some supporters appeared sympathetic to his situation, while others were much more direct about his chances of reaching the postseason roster.“It sucks to be him, but damn.”Another fan kept the reaction short, writing, “Well…that’s a bummer.”The frustration became stronger in other responses. One fan wrote, “This guy won’t sniff the playoff roster… Back to the lab you go” Another added, “Bad time of year to be a total liability.”Other comments went beyond criticism of Kyle Harrison’s performance and included personal and offensive attacks. Those reactions highlighted just how frustrated some fans have become after watching his recent decline.The frustration is tied to how sharply Kyle Harrison’s season has changed. He finished May with a 1.57 ERA, putting himself in the conversation as one of the Milwaukee Brewers’ promising pitching pieces. Kyle Harrison also had a 1.93 ERA through the end of June when his eight-run outing against the Oakland Athletics in Las Vegas was removed from the calculation.Then came the injury and the decline.Kyle Harrison spent much of July on the injured list because of a left forearm injury. After returning, his fastball did not have the same effectiveness. His struggles became increasingly difficult to overlook in August and September.Over his last four outings, Kyle Harrison has allowed 21 earned runs in nine innings for a 21.00 ERA.Against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Kyle Harrison recorded only five outs. A two-out walk to Ronny Simon in the second inning began a sequence in which seven consecutive Pirates hitters reached safely.Fans are running out of patience as Kyle Harrison searches for answersThe numbers make the difference between Kyle Harrison’s two halves particularly striking. From March through June, he posted a 2.57 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and .213 opponent batting average. From July through September, those figures climbed to a 7.90 ERA, 2.01 WHIP and .344 opponent batting average.The concern is not only about results. The Milwaukee Brewers are also trying to identify what has changed physically.Kyle Harrison’s average four-seam fastball against Pittsburgh was 95.3 mph, slightly above his season average. However, its vertical movement remained below his normal level.“The heater hasn’t been as ‘poppy,’” Kyle Harrison said. “I’m feeling good, but I need to dial that thing in.”Pat Murphy has acknowledged the challenge facing the young left-hander.“His delivery has to be impeccable, and his mental state has to be improving, because when you go through a stretch like this, it’s very tough to get yourself together,” Pat Murphy said.Kyle Harrison, however, has refused to give up.“I’m not going to give in, not going to give up,” Kyle Harrison said. “I’m going to keep working and fighting.”Pat Murphy has confirmed that Kyle Harrison will pitch again during the Milwaukee Brewers’ final nine regular-season games, although his role remains undecided.That gives Kyle Harrison another opportunity to change the conversation. For now, the fan reactions show the pressure surrounding the left-hander as the Milwaukee Brewers move closer to October.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: George Springer’s Toronto Blue Jays story takes a new turn as the playoff race heats up
articles.summary: MLB News: George Springer’s place in Toronto Blue Jays lineup has taken a new turn at a time when every game carries extra weight. After spending the recent str.
articles.body: George Springer’s place in Toronto Blue Jays lineup has taken a new turn at a time when every game carries extra weight. After spending the recent stretch batting second, veteran designated hitter George Springer has been moved into the cleanup spot for Toronto Blue Jays’ series finale against Detroit Tigers. The change comes after George Springer found some rhythm at the plate, collecting at least one hit in five straight games. Three of those outings were multi-hit performances. For Toronto Blue Jays, which is trying to stay in the American League postseason picture, the decision puts one of its experienced hitters in a bigger run-producing role.George Springer’s new cleanup role gives Toronto Blue Jays a fresh sparkThe timing of the move makes it especially interesting. Toronto Blue Jays entered Detroit Tigers series needing results but lost the first two games, adding pressure to the series finale.George Springer had been batting second during his recent run of consistency. Toronto Blue Jays manager John Schneider then moved George Springer into the cleanup position, giving veteran hitter a different place in the heart of the order.The move puts George Springer in a spot where his experience and recent production could become even more important. It also comes after a difficult stretch in which his playing time was affected by a lingering shoulder issue.George Springer has gradually taken on a different role with Toronto Blue Jays. He has moved from being an everyday outfielder toward spending more time as a designated hitter, but his presence in the lineup remains valuable.His recent numbers at the plate provide a clear reason for the change. George Springer has recorded a hit in five consecutive games, with three multi-hit performances during that stretch. That consistency has given John Schneider another reason to trust him in an important part of the batting order.For Toronto Blue Jays, the goal is simple. The team needs its experienced hitters to produce while the postseason race enters a crucial stage.George Springer’s recent form gives Toronto Blue Jays another reason to trust him in the playoff raceGeorge Springer’s 2026 season has included both steady production and uncertainty about what comes next. In 118 games, George Springer has recorded 110 hits, 57 runs, 15 home runs and 52 RBIs across 434 at-bats. He is batting .253 with a .746 OPS.Those numbers only tell part of George Springer’s role. His experience also matters for a Toronto clubhouse that has undergone major changes during the season.That was particularly visible around the trade deadline. George Springer was among the veterans who could have been moved because he was playing on an expiring contract. Instead, Toronto Blue Jays kept him, along with Max Scherzer and Shane Bieber.The deadline also brought an emotional moment involving George Springer and teammates who were leaving Toronto. Daulton Varsho revealed that he, George Springer and Kevin Gausman shared an emotional goodbye before Kevin Gausman was traded to Chicago Cubs.“I felt it last night with Gausman on the plane,” Daulton Varsho said, according to MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson. “We broke down and he cried with me and George.”George Springer remained with Toronto Blue Jays while several familiar faces moved on. Months later, his role has changed again, this time on the field.Moving George Springer into the cleanup spot gives him another opportunity to influence a team fighting for October. Whether the change lasts beyond Detroit Tigers series remains to be seen, but the timing is significant.With the postseason race tightening, Toronto Blue Jays are turning to experience and recent form. George Springer now has a bigger place in that effort.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Freddie Freeman’s wife Chelsea Freeman steps beyond Los Angeles Dodgers spotlight with a story of family, style and purpose
articles.summary: MLB News: Freddie Freeman’s wife Chelsea Freeman has built a life that reaches well beyond the baseball field. A recent social media appearance brought fresh at.
articles.body: Freddie Freeman’s wife Chelsea Freeman has built a life that reaches well beyond the baseball field. A recent social media appearance brought fresh attention to her style, but the moment also offered a glimpse into the world she has created away from the Los Angeles Dodgers spotlight. Chelsea Freeman is a mother, businesswoman and familiar presence around Major League Baseball through her husband’s career. From raising three sons with Freddie Freeman to appearing at MLB events and developing her own business interests, her story has continued to grow alongside one of baseball’s biggest names.Chelsea Freeman’s latest moment showed the personal style she has made her ownChelsea Freeman recently shared a series of photos wearing a bright yellow mini dress while promoting FashionPass, a US-based clothing and accessories rental service. Her look included summer sandals, a colorful bag, rings and a diamond bracelet, while her makeup remained light and natural.The photos were taken at a luxury property overlooking the sea. Three images showed Chelsea Freeman outside in the sunlight, while another offered an indoor view of the elegant setting.The post carried a simple message that matched the mood of the photos.“A little sunshine in dress form,” Chelsea Freeman captioned her IG post.The FashionPass collaboration also reflected another side of Chelsea Freeman’s public presence. She has developed a strong social media following by sharing fashion, family moments, travel memories and glimpses of everyday life.That has allowed her identity to extend beyond being known simply as Freddie Freeman’s wife. Her online presence often gives fans a closer look at the person supporting one of baseball’s most recognizable players while also maintaining interests of her own.Chelsea Freeman has also remained connected to the wider MLB community. During the 2026 All-Star Game red carpet, she took on an interviewer role and spoke with several baseball stars’ wives and girlfriends.Family and business have shaped Chelsea Freeman’s life away from the DodgersChelsea Freeman and Freddie Freeman began dating in June 2011 after meeting while Chelsea Freeman was attending the University of Central Florida. The couple became engaged in January 2014 and married on November 22, 2014, at the St. Regis Bal Harbour in Miami Beach, Florida.The couple have three sons. Frederick Charles Freeman II, known as Charlie, was born in September 2016. Brandon John Freeman was born in December 2020, while Maximus Turner Freeman was born in February 2021.Motherhood has remained an important part of Chelsea Freeman’s life. She frequently shares family moments online, while her children have also been seen supporting Freddie Freeman during his baseball career.Her connection to baseball became particularly visible during the 2026 All-Star Game. Chelsea Freeman interviewed Olivia Dunne, the girlfriend of Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes, during a lighthearted Q&A. Olivia Dunne revealed that she carries her identification in her purse so she can get a drink, prompting a laugh from Chelsea Freeman.Chelsea Freeman also spoke with Kate Upton, wife of Justin Verlander. Their conversation included questions about fashion at home and what Justin Verlander might have done if he had not become a professional baseball player.Away from those MLB appearances, Chelsea Freeman has pursued her own business path. She founded the Chelsea Freeman Collection, an online boutique offering game-day clothing and merchandise connected to Los Angeles and Atlanta.Before that, Chelsea Freeman worked as a real estate agent with Keller Williams. She had also worked as a model during her college years.Her journey has therefore taken several directions. She has experienced the demands of being married to a professional baseball player, built a family with Freddie Freeman and developed interests that belong to her alone.The latest social media moment may have brought Chelsea Freeman back into the spotlight, but her story is much bigger than one post. He doesn't qualify for the ERA or WHIP rankings because most of his starts don't see him go overly deep into games. He has only completed six or more innings in 12 of 28 starts this season. He has been superb at home with a 2.09 ERA in 13 starts. The Cubs faced him once this season and got two earned runs off of him over 5.2 innings. articles.title: Aaron Judge Injured, Latest Updates on Yankees Star's Timeline to Return Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: Just over a week after he returned from a rib injury that kept him out for most of the season, Aaron Judge is heading back to the injured list.
articles.body:
Just over a week after he returned from a rib injury that kept him out for most of the season, Aaron Judge is heading back to the injured list.

Judge is being placed on the 10-day IL with a calf strain, the New York Yankees announced Friday.

Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters he wouldn't place a timeline on Judge's calf strain. When asked if the slugger would be back for the postseason, Boone replied, "I don't know."

Judge left Wednesday's game against the Minnesota Twins in the sixth inning because of right lower leg tightness. He said after the game that he felt something during the first inning and eventually decided he should come out.

Judge went 0-for-2 with a pair of strikeouts before he exited the game. Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for him.

Judge suffered a rib injury in late May and missed more than three months of action, finally making his return last Tuesday against the Colorado Rockies. Since returning, he's gone 4-for-21 with a home run and three RBI, clearly still working his way back to 100 percent.

After his return, the three-time AL MVP addressed having to get back into shape while simultaneously helping the Yankees fight for ideal playoff seeding.

"I get paid to do this, so I gotta go do it," Judge told reporters. "That's the end of it. I get paid to go out there and give my best to the New York Yankees and these fans. So, you get paid to win games so you gotta keep going out there and winning games."

Luckily for Judge, New York managed to stay afloat during his absence. The Yankees are sitting in second place in the AL East and secured a spot in the postseason earlier this week.

The Bronx Bombers are six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox and should be able to secure the top wild-card spot.

Even though New York has guaranteed a spot in the playoffs, Judge's injury is worrisome. The Yankees may have managed when he was gone, but making a World Series push without their star would be a different story.

With Judge heading back to the injured list, the Yankees will hope their star slugger can return to the lineup sooner rather than later as New York battles for playoff position in the AL East.

articles.title: Nationals sign pitcher Cade Cavalli to 4-year contract extension for reported $47 million with team option for 2031
articles.summary: In his first season as a full-time starter, Cavalli ranks fourth among NL pitchers in strikeouts and eighth in ERA.
articles.body:
The Washington Nationals have signed pitcher Cade Cavalli to a four-year contract extension, the team announced on Friday . The deal includes a club option for 2031.

The contract will pay Cavalli a guaranteed $47 million, but could be worth up to $70 million if the 2031 option is picked up, The Athletic's Spencer Nusbaum reports .

Cavalli, 28, is eighth among National League starting pitchers with a 3.12 ERA in 31 starts. In his first season as a full-time starter, he has 194 strikeouts (fourth among NL pitchers) in 164 2/3 innings with a 12-5 record.

During the second half of the season, Cavalli has excelled, posting a 2.05 ERA with a 7-1 record and 84 strikeouts in 66 innings.

The Nationals' 2020 first-round pick (No. 22 overall) out of Oklahoma, Cavalli was in his second year of arbitration eligibility with a $4 million club option for 2027, according to Spotrac . He missed the entire 2023 season after undergoing Tommy John surgery and only made 10 starts last year while working his way back.

With the contract extension, Washington buys out the 2027 option and Cavalli's final two arbitration seasons up to the 2030 season. The deal also includes a team option for 2031 in what would be Cavalli's first year of free agency.

After striking out Contreras during their 8-1 win on June 30, Cavalli yelled "Sit down, boy" which the 11-year veteran didn't take kindly. The Red Sox and Nationals benches and bullpens each emptied, with several players engaged in pushing and shoving, while Contreras tried to throw his helmet at Cavalli.

Both players were initially given seven-game suspensions by MLB, but Cavalli had his penalty reduced to five games and Contreras served a six-game punishment.

The last multiyear contract extension the Nationals signed a player to was catcher Keibert Ruiz , who inked an eight-year, $50 million agreement in 2023. This is the first long-term contract offered to a player under president of baseball operations Paul Toboni, who took that position a year ago .

At 71-82, the Nationals are fourth in the NL East but could still finish last in the division. Since winning the World Series in 2019 , Washington has finished either fourth or fifth for the past seven seasons. That could continue next season with one of MLB's smaller payrolls even while building around players like Ruiz and Cavalli.

articles.title: Aaron Judge to hit IL due to calf strain, can't return until Yankees' final game of regular season
articles.summary: A rough season for the Yankees' superstar just got rougher.
articles.body:
New York Yankees star Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list due to a right calf strain, the club announced Friday .

Assuming the roster move is backdated to Thursday, the day after Judge's last on-field appearance, the three-time AL MVP won't be eligible to return until Sept. 27, the day of the Yankees' final game of the regular season. Of course, it's unclear if he will be ready to play by then.

Per Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News, the Yankees plan to call up outfielder Max Schuemann from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre as the corresponding move for Judge.

Judge came off the IL only 10 days earlier after missing three months due to a stress fracture in his ribs. He has played in seven games since then, going 4-for-23 with 1 homer and 13 strikeouts.

This injury popped up on Wednesday, when Judge left a game due to what he described as stiffness in his lower right leg. Per MLB.com , Judge didn't point to any one play causing the issue. Rather, he described it as the kind of issue that arises after a long layoff like his IL stint:

"I feel like you deal with this every spring training. You know, usually at the start of the season once you start ramping up again, things pop up, and that's where we've been," Judge said. "Thankfully, this whole time coming back, nothing's really nagged us. So hopefully it's just one little thing and then we're back out there soon."

Unfortunately, the injury appears to not be one little thing.

Judge has won AL MVP in three of the past four seasons, but this year has not gone according to plan. He got off to a slow start by his standards, slashing only .248/.375/.533 until the Yankees placed him on the IL in early June. Those struggles were partially due to the rib injury, which he reportedly tried to play through for six weeks.

Judge didn't return to the lineup until Sept. 8, and now he's going back on the shelf. Going forward, he represents an enormous unknown for the Yankees, who sit second in the AL East at 88-64. They are currently on pace for a second straight wild-card series clash with the Boston Red Sox.

At best, Judge could return right before the playoffs. At worst, he might have already played his final game of 2026.

Not counting his cup of coffee in 2016 or the COVID-shortened 2020 season, Judge has never played in fewer than the 66 games he's seen in 2026 or posted an OPS+ lower than this year's 140 (which is still very good). That adds up to a career-worst season for Judge at 34 years old.

articles.title: Livvy Dunne Dismisses Fantasy Baseball Manager's Paul Skenes Request With 'South Park' Meme

It's hard to argue Skenes hasn't helped fantasy teams this season. He's obviously not pitching as well as he did in 2024 or 2025, but his 3.78 ERA and 185 strikeouts in 162 innings is far from terrible.

This has been a strange season for many pitchers. Not many people would have guessed in April that Jesús Luzardo, Drew Rasmussen and Parker Messick were going to be top-eight fantasy starters.

articles.title: Dodgers Owner Mark Walter Sued Over Alleged Failure to Disclose Federal Probe to Policyholders
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns have been sued, alleging they failed to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers while directing policyholders' money into Walter's other companies.
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns have been sued, alleging they failed to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers while directing policyholders' money into Walter's other companies.

The lawsuit lists Walter, Delaware Life Insurance Co., Clear Spring Life and Annuity, TWG Global Holdings and Walter's Guggenheim Partners investment firm as defendants.

Ira Rosner, a 67-year-old Florida man, brought the class-action lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Miami on Wednesday. He purchased a policy from Delaware Life in April and he had until late May to withdraw his money without penalty. However, the company did not disclose the investigation to him until June

Ranking Every Team's Best Rookie in 2026 🔢

Rosner is seeking a jury trial in the lawsuit that seeks damages for negligent misrepresentation, breach of contract and aiding and abetting fraud.

TWG Global didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.

Walter has been under investigation since last year by the U.S. Attorney's Office in Manhattan and the Securities and Exchange Commission following a whistleblower complaint regarding alleged misrepresented loans made between companies within his business portfolio.

TWG Global Holdings is the holding company through which Walter controls Delaware Life, Clear Spring Life and Annuity Co. and his stake in Guggenheim Partners. TWG Global denied any wrongdoing involving the probe in a statement last month.

Walter and co-owner Todd Boehly sold their stakes in English Premier League club Chelsea this week. Last month, Walter agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers in a surprise move less than a year after buying the NBA franchise from the Buss family. The deal is under review by the league.

The Dodgers have been adamant that Walter has no plans to sell the baseball team.

articles.title: Jared Young Injury Update, Latest on Mets 1B's Status After Hospitalization for Collision
articles.summary: New York Mets first baseman Jared Young left the team's matchup with the Philadelphia Phillies on a stretcher after colliding with starting pitcher Nolan McLean on Thursday.
articles.body:
New York Mets first baseman Jared Young left the team's matchup with the Philadelphia Phillies on a stretcher after colliding with starting pitcher Nolan McLean on Thursday.

He was later transported to the hospital for further examination, the Mets announced.

Mets interim manager Andy Green told reporters Friday that Young is doing "as good as expected or could be hoped for." All the tests he underwent went well, though he has short-term memory loss and bad headaches.

In the top of the sixth inning, Phillies outfielder Justin Crawford hit a ground ball towards first base.

As McLean ran to first to field the ball, his leg appeared to collide with Young's head as he was simultaneously leaning down to pick up the ball.

Young was replaced by Mark Vientos in New York's lineup after exiting the contest.

While the Mets have failed to meet expectations this season and sit at the bottom of the National League East standings with a 69-83 record, the play of Young has been a silver lining for the team.

Although he was initially brought in by New York as a depth piece in 2024 and played just 44 total MLB games heading into this year, he was suiting up in his 103rd appearance of the season on Thursday.

Young has racked up nine home runs, 17 doubles and 39 RBI while slashing .266/.330/.429 in 2026.

He's particularly excelled against right-handed pitching, owning a .797 OPS in 250 at-bats against right-handers this season.

Young recently received praise from Mets director of hitting Jeff Albert for his efforts.

"He's been great," Albert said regarding Young, per Tim Britton and Will Sammon of The Athletic. "I can't say enough good things about what he's done in the box, defense, in the cage, in the room. Just really a pro all the way around. It's great to see him take advantage of the opportunity. The guys that know him, I don't think it's surprising."

As the Mets continue to navigate through their 2026 campaign, the health of Young will be something to monitor moving forward.

articles.title: Updated 2026 MLB Playoffs Bracket Picture and Standings After Braves Clinch Berth
articles.summary: After a one year absence, the Atlanta Braves are back in the playoffs.
articles.body:
After a one year absence, the Atlanta Braves are back in the playoffs.

The Braves clinched a playoff berth on Friday with a 6-2 win over the Houston Astros.

After a run of seven consecutive playoff appearances from 2018 to '24, the Braves had a disappointing 2025 in large part due to injuries to key players. Ronald Acuña Jr., Austin Riley, Sean Murphy, Spencer Schwellenbach and Spencer Strider all missed significant time last year.

This season wasn't dramatically better for the Braves on the injury front, but having Chris Sale still throwing like an ace and a breakout year from Drake Baldwin helped offset a lot of those issues.

Sale, in particular, has a great case to win the NL Cy Young award for the second time in three years. He is on pace to finish with a 2.18 ERA in his age-37 season.

Pitching is the strength for this Braves team that ranks fourth in MLB with a 3.64 ERA. The lineup has been solid with the eighth-most runs scored, but Acuña and Ozzie Albies will need to pick things up in October if this team hopes to challenge the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies in the NL.

The 2026 MLB playoffs begin with the wild card round on Sept. 29, followed by the division series starting Oct. 3.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Minor League Player of the Year for Every MLB Organization
articles.summary: As the 2026 MLB season winds to a close, the minor league campaign is also wrapping up this weekend, making this the perfect time to recognize the top prospect performers of the MiLB season.
articles.body:
As the 2026 MLB season winds to a close, the minor league campaign is also wrapping up this weekend, making this the perfect time to recognize the top prospect performers of the MiLB season.

The goal is to identify each team's most impressive prospect based solely on their 2026 production. Future potential, past performance and where they stand in prospect rankings were not a factor, though age relative to level was an important data point.

Not all of these players offer the same type of long-term ceiling, but in 2026, they were the most productive prospects in their respective farm systems and have earned B/R's Minor League Player of the Year honors for their efforts.

Both position players and pitchers were eligible to be the pick for their respective team. Only players who still carry prospect status were considered, so guys who got off to a strong start in the minors and then spent enough time in the big leagues to exceed rookie eligibility limits were not eligible.

Stats (A+/AA): 24 GS, 2.27 ERA, 0.90 WHIP, 30 BB, 149 K, 131.0 IP

With a lanky 6'8" frame, a mid-90s fastball and a terrific changeup, Dzierwa has exceeded expectations since going in the second round of the 2025 draft out of Michigan State. His stuff plays up thanks to a deceptive arm slot, and with a 2.29 ERA in 90.1 innings at Double-A he is on the fast track to Baltimore.

Stats (AA/AAA): 115 G, .320/.397/.551, 53 XBH (24 HR), 9 SB

Arias hit .278/.335/.388 with eight home runs in 116 games across three minor league levels in 2025, and his offensive upside and polished glove at shortstop were enough to make him a consensus Top 100 prospect. The 20-year-old's offensive game took off this year, and now it looks like he could push for the Red Sox shortstop job next spring.

Stats (A/A+): 112 G, .287/.361/.512, 49 XBH (24 HR), 41 SB

Lovich was a 16th-round pick in 2025 out of Missouri where he hit .357/.430/.622 with 12 home runs as a junior, albeit with 52 strikeouts in 51 games. The swing-and-miss remains, as he has a 28.6 percent strikeout rate this season, but he has filled up the stat sheet with 21 doubles, 24 home runs, 89 RBI, 86 runs scored and 41 steals while seeing time at shortstop, third base and center field.

Stats (A+/AA): 116 G, .315/.419/.546, 52 XBH (22 HR), 44 SB

One of the best pure hitters in the minors with a 55-power, 60-speed toolbox to boot, Gillen has fully showcased the offensive upside that made him the No. 18 overall pick in the 2024 draft. His 13.9 percent walk rate and .419 on-base percentage while reaching Double-A at the age of 20 speak to how advanced his bat is already.

Stats (AA/AAA): 100 G, .294/.417/.602, 51 XBH (28 HR), 7 SB

Keys crushed 28 home runs in 100 games in the minors this season, including a gaudy .303/.422/.622 line with 14 long balls over 226 plate appearances at the Triple-A level. He is a bat-first prospect with limited athleticism, but he has hit his way to the majors this year, going 9-for-45 with two home runs in limited action.

Stats (A+/AA): 132 G, .251/.380/.550, 69 XBH (37 HR), 17 SB

Bonemer quickly established himself as a top prospect with an .874 OPS and 46 extra-base hits in 107 games between Single-A and High-A in his pro debut in 2025. His 161 strikeouts and 27.1 percent strikeout rate will need to improve as he climbs the ladder, but a 37-homer season while reaching Double-A as a 20-year-old is tough to ignore.

Cleveland Guardians: 1B Ralphy Velazquez

Stats (AA/AAA): 119 G, .293/.381/.555, 58 XBH (29 HR), 2 SB

Velazquez has some of the best raw power of any prospect, and more than enough hit tool to fully utilize it at the next level. The 21-year-old put up an absurd .356/.433/.867 line with 15 home runs in 23 games in August, and he should have a real shot at an Opening Day roster spot in 2027.

Stats (A/AAA): 110 G, .301/.386/.488, 42 XBH (17 HR), 5 SB

After tallying 52 extra-base hits over 122 games in the upper levels of the minors in 2025, Anderson posted an absurd .447/.609/.809 line over 69 plate appearances in the Arizona Fall League. He has continued to rake at Triple-A this year, and he could be the heir to Gleyber Torres at second base if he walks in free agency.

Stats (A+): 25 GS, 4.01 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, 28 BB, 139 K, 116.2 IP

Shields became the first teenage pitcher with more than 115 innings pitched and a strikeout rate above 29 percent since 2017, and just the sixth to do it since 2007, joining an exclusive group that includes Clayton Kershaw and Madison Bumgarner. He was taken in the second round of the same 2024 draft, when Jac Caglianone was the team's first-round selection.

Stats (A+/AA): 116 G, .312/.392/.455, 42 XBH (12 HR), 50 SB

Houston was a three-year starter at shortstop for Wake Forest and the No. 16 overall pick in the 2025 draft, and while his reliable glove gave him a high floor, his bat has him looking more and more like a future everyday option. With a strikeout rate below 20 percent, a walk rate above 11 percent and 50 steals in 59 attempts, he can make an offensive impact even without plus power.

Stats (A+/AA/AAA): 138 G, .308/.412/.488, 51 XBH (22 HR), 13 SB

After posting a 1.130 OPS with 54 home runs in three seasons at the University of Indiana, Taylor has continued to look like a future middle-of-the-order run producer. The bulk of his damage this season came at the Double-A level, where he logged a .943 OPS with 30 extra-base hits in 68 games, and he is one of 18 minor leaguers with 100 RBI.

Stats (A+/AA/AAA): 121 G, .247/.387/.526, 56 XBH (32 HR), 32 SB

Schiavone is the first catcher to record a 30/30 season in the minors since Willie Royster in 1981, and they are the only two to do it since 1946, according to MLB.com . The 23-year-old is still developing behind the plate, but he has the arm to control the running game with a 33 percent caught stealing rate over 68 starts behind the dish.

Stats (A/A+): 118 G, .289/.391/.456, 49 XBH (12 HR), 53 SB

Alvarez has a 55-hit, 60-power offensive profile, and room to grow into significantly more power as his 6'3", 190-pound frame fills out. He hit .296/.396/.479 with 42 extra-base hits and 46 steals in 96 games at Single-A, and has held his own over 22 games since being bumped up to High-A at the age of 19.

Stats (AA): 22 GS, 3.73 ERA, 1.13 WHIP, 16 BB, 128 K, 101.1 IP

Kade Anderson (18 GS, 1.06 ERA, 135 K, 93.1 IP) was a man among boys during his time in the minors, but he has spent the last month in the majors, and that leaves Sloan as the clear choice. A top-10 prospect leaguewide in his own right, Sloan's 128-to-16 strikeout-to-walk ratio as a 20-year-old in Double-A highlights his legitimate frontline upside.

Stats (A+/AA): 116 G, .315/.401/.586, 62 XBH (27 HR), 9 SB

Perich hit .382/.492/.572 with more walks (34) than strikeouts (23) during his junior season at Lehigh, but hit just six home runs that year and 15 total in 499 plate appearances over three seasons. His power surge this year has elevated his prospect status, and he made a clean jump to Double-A with a .981 OPS and 16 home runs in 78 games since he was promoted.

Ranking Every Team's Best Rookie in 2026 🔢

Stats (A+/AA): 128 G, .249/.350/.456, 49 XBH (26 HR), 56 SB

Two years after going in the 20th round of the 2024 draft, Hartman is now the consensus No. 1 prospect in the Atlanta farm system. He turned 20 years old in June, but has already reached Double-A after hitting .273/.364/.525 with 43 extra-base hits and 38 steals in 94 games at High-A to start the year.

Stats (A+/AA/AAA): 124 G, .271/.411/.572, 64 XBH (35 HR), 27 SB

Compton logged the three hardest-hit balls in Draft Combine history before going in the second round of the 2025 draft, rebuilding some stock after a disappointing redshirt sophomore campaign at Arizona State. The loud raw power has been on full display this season with 35 home runs in 124 games over three levels, and while his 189 strikeouts are a red flag, they are accompanied by 103 walks.

Stats (A+/AA): 105 G, .273/.371/.431, 38 XBH (13 HR), 45 SB

Voit has actually put up better numbers since he was promoted from High-A to Double-A, hitting .347/.430/.517 with 15 extra-base hits in 29 games since making the jump. The 21-year-old has plus tools across the board and a real chance to stick at shortstop, where his athleticism and strong arm are a clean fit.

Stats (AA): 118 G, .267/.410/.517, 52 XBH (26 HR), 30 SB

Rincon hit .181/.304/.298 with six home runs in 84 games at High-A last season, but he has seen an offensive explosion this year. A hitter-friendly environment at Reading is part of the power surge, but he also has an .873 OPS and 11 long balls on the road. An uptick in offensive impact alongside his standout glove makes him the pick here over an impressive first full season from Gage Wood.

Stats (AA/AAA): 109 G, .306/.385/.517, 48 XBH (20 HR), 15 SB
